```{r, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>", eval = FALSE, purl = FALSE)
```

`shad_data_table()` renders a data frame as a shadcn-styled, client-side table
with sorting, filtering, paging, and row selection. Everything runs in the
browser: the whole frame is serialised once, and interaction never round-trips
to R unless you ask for it.

It is an *input*, not an output. Place it in the UI like any other bound
component and read its state with `input$<id>`.

## The minimum

```{r}
library(shiny)
library(shadshiny)

ui <- page_shad(
  shad_data_table("tbl", mtcars)
)

server <- function(input, output, session) {
  observe(print(input$tbl))
}
```

Column names become headers, row names are dropped, and each column gets a
default cell renderer based on its type: numerics are right-aligned and
formatted, dates print ISO, logicals become check marks, and factors and
characters print as text.

## Reading state

`input$<id>` is a list describing what the user is looking at:

| Field | Type | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `selected` | character vector | Row keys, in selection order, and persisting across pages. By default a key is the row's 1-based index in the data you passed, as a string — so `as.integer(input$tbl$selected)` indexes the frame. Set `row_key` to use a column instead. |
| `sort` | list of `{column, direction}` | Active sort keys, outermost first. `direction` is `"asc"` or `"desc"`. |
| `filter` | list | `global` (string) plus one entry per filtered column. |
| `page` | integer | Current 1-based page. |
| `pageSize` | integer | Rows per page. |

```{r}
server <- function(input, output, session) {
  chosen <- reactive({
    keys <- input$tbl$selected
    if (!length(keys)) mtcars else mtcars[as.integer(keys), , drop = FALSE]
  })
  output$n <- renderText(sprintf("%d rows selected", nrow(chosen())))
}
```

Because the default key is a row index into the *original* frame, you never
have to reconstruct the client's sort or filter in R to know which rows the
user picked.

## Table options

```{r}
shad_data_table(
  "tbl", sales,
  selection         = "multiple",   # "none", "single", or "multiple"
  filter            = "both",       # "none", "global", "columns", or "both"
  page_size         = 25,
  page_sizes        = c(10, 25, 50, 100),
  column_visibility = TRUE,         # a dropdown to show/hide columns
  sticky_header     = TRUE,
  max_height        = "32rem",
  empty             = "Nothing matches that filter."
)
```

With `filter = "both"` the table gets a search box above it *and* a filter
input under each header; `"global"` and `"columns"` give you one or the other.

`shad_data_table()` serialises the whole frame, so it guards the size for you:
over 100,000 cells it warns, and over 1,000,000 it errors. Pre-aggregate or
page server-side before you get there.

## Columns and formatting

Pass `columns` — a named list of `shad_col()` specs, keyed by column name.
Anything you leave out keeps its default.

```{r}
shad_data_table(
  "tbl", sales,
  columns = list(
    order  = shad_col("Order #", width = "8rem"),
    amount = shad_col("Amount", format = shad_fmt_number(2, prefix = "$")),
    margin = shad_col("Margin", format = shad_fmt_percent(1)),
    date   = shad_col("Date", format = shad_fmt_date("%b %d, %Y")),
    status = shad_col("Status", format = shad_fmt_badge(
      c(paid = "default", pending = "secondary", refunded = "destructive")
    )),
    notes  = shad_col(visible = FALSE)
  )
)
```

`shad_col()` takes `header` (the first argument — the displayed label), plus
`width`, `align`, `sortable`, `filterable`, `visible`, `html`, and one of
`format` or `cell`. `format` and `cell` are mutually exclusive, and neither
combines with `html = TRUE` (which passes the column's strings through as raw
HTML — only do that with values you generated).

The bundled formatters are:

| Formatter | Renders |
|---|---|
| `shad_fmt_number(digits, big_mark, prefix, suffix)` | Fixed-decimal number. |
| `shad_fmt_percent(digits)` | Value × 100 with a `%` suffix. |
| `shad_fmt_date(format)` | `format()`-style date string, e.g. `"%b %d, %Y"`. |
| `shad_fmt_badge(map)` | `shad_badge()` per value; `map` is value → variant. |

Formatters keep the raw value as the sort key, so a `$1,200.00` cell still
sorts numerically and a `"Mar 03"` cell still sorts chronologically.

### Custom cells

When a formatter isn't enough, give the column a `cell` function. It is called
once per row with the column value and the whole row, and returns a tag or a
string:

```{r}
shad_col("Owner", cell = function(value, row) {
  shad_item(
    shad_avatar(src = row$avatar_url, fallback = substr(value, 1, 2)),
    shad_p(value)
  )
})
```

Cell functions run in R at render time, not on the client — so they cost one
call per visible row of the frame you pass, and they cannot see later filter
state. Keep them cheap.

## Updating from the server

```{r}
observeEvent(input$refresh, {
  update_shad_data_table("tbl", data = fetch_latest())
})
```

`update_shad_data_table()` replaces the rows and can patch `selected`, `page`,
`page_size`, and `loading`. Pass `columns` alongside `data` to re-apply your
formatters and `cell` functions to the new rows. The client keeps its sort and
filter, so a refresh doesn't yank the view out from under the user; the column
*headers* and visibility are fixed at UI-construction time.

## Loading state

```{r}
shad_data_table("tbl", NULL, loading = TRUE)
# later:
update_shad_data_table("tbl", data = result(), loading = FALSE)
```

`loading = TRUE` renders skeleton rows at the current page size.

## When to keep `DT`

`shad_data_table()` ships the whole frame to the browser. That is the right
trade for tables up to roughly the tens of thousands of rows. Past that — or
when you need server-side paging, Excel export, or the JS DataTables plugin
ecosystem — keep `DT::datatable()` and style its container.
